title: Software Engineer, Enterprise Product
description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Software Engineer, Enterprise Product, you’ll solve the hardest problems standing between Ramp and the world’s largest and most complex companies — shaping and shipping the product capabilities that unlock our growth upmarket. You'll be part of our Core FDE org, which is an agent-first, high-pace, customer-facing engineering team. On FDE, you will interact directly with customers and deliver solutions end to end — understanding pain points, shaping product decisions, and building agents that autonomously expand Ramp's capabilities.

Check out our Engineering Blog https://engineering.ramp.com/ and FDE post https://engineering.ramp.com/post/forward-deployed-engineering for more context on our work!

 


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Deliver software end to end that meet the needs of our largest customers — understanding user pain points, scoping product specs, and building agents that autonomously implement solutions.

 - Collaborate closely with Sales, Solutions, Customer Success, and Account Management to close deals, activate customers, and expand the value Ramp provides over time.

 - Drive the core product engineering roadmap through our embedding model — specializing within a core product area to develop deep domain expertise and make prioritization calls on when to build a custom solution vs. accelerate a broader initiative.


WHAT YOU NEED

 - 3+ years of software engineering experience preferred

 - Extensive experience building with and for agents

 - Track record of shipping high-quality products at scale

 - Comfort and excitement to be customer-facing

 - Desire to work in a fast-paced environment, continuously grow, and master your craft




BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL)

 - Flexible PTO

 - Centralized home-office equipment ordering

 - Health and wellness stipend

 - Budget for intra-office travel

 - Weekly coffee stipend




UNITED STATES

 - 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

 - One Medical annual membership

 - 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

 - Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

 - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

 - Pet insurance

 - In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

 - Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)
   
   


CANADA

 - Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

 - Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

 - Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

 - Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

 - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

 - Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health




UNITED KINGDOM

 - Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

 - Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

 - Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

 - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay




REFERRAL INSTRUCTIONS

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 


OTHER NOTICES

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com http://Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

title: Software Engineer, Identity Infrastructure
description:
About the Team

The Identity Infrastructure Engineering team builds the identity and access systems that OpenAI’s researchers, engineers, and internal teams rely on to protect critical systems and data.

We partner with Research, Applied Engineering, Infrastructure, IT, and Security to make secure access practical across cloud and internal environments.

About the Role

We’re looking for a hands-on software engineer to design and build high-scale, high-throughput secure access proxies and the distributed systems behind them. These are tier-zero services: researchers, engineers, and agents depend on them to reach critical infrastructure safely and reliably.

You’ll work at the intersection of networking, distributed systems, and infrastructure security, building the serving paths and control-plane integrations that connect identities to resources. Teleport is a core part of the current platform; the role also includes credential brokers, policy enforcement, and developer-facing integrations.

You’ll own the services you build from design and implementation through production. That means understanding human, agent, and workload traffic, improving throughput and tail latency, making authorization decisions auditable, and designing for safe multi-region rollout and recovery. We’re looking for someone who can turn a demanding security requirement into software that works well at scale and is straightforward for other engineers to use.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and implement secure access proxies, gateways, and credential brokers that provide narrowly scoped, auditable access to infrastructure and internal services while reducing standing privileges..

 - Integrate identity and access policy across clients, proxies, and target systems so approved permissions take effect promptly and access expires or is revoked when required. Ensure correct behavior when policy is stale or sessions remain active.

 - Build observability that explains the end-to-end access path: latency, errors, saturation, authorization decisions, and identity attribution, without leaking credentials.

 - Engineer safe multi-region rollouts, canaries, rollback, failover, and recovery. Validate changes with realistic test environments, load tests, and failure testing.

 - Keep core access services reliable, performant, and maintainable. Own production support, maintenance, upgrades, and incident recovery; ship durable fixes that reduce recurring failures, alert noise, and manual work.

 - Make secure access easy to adopt through reusable APIs, client tooling, diagnostics, and self-service workflows. Lead migrations that preserve critical workflows, with tested rollback and recovery paths and clear ownership across Infrastructure, Security, and SRE.

You might thrive in this role if you: 

 - Have built and operated production backend, proxy, networking, or infrastructure services with demanding scale or availability requirements.

 - Have practical networking depth and can reason about HTTP, TCP, TLS, DNS, routing, and load balancing across real request paths.

 - Can explain how you handled performance bottlenecks, partial failures, multi-region deployment, or a difficult production change in a system you personally built.

 - Understand authentication, authorization, least privilege, trust boundaries, credential handling, and the consequences of an access-control failure.

 - Have strong software engineering fundamentals and experience with Go, Rust, Python, or similar languages.

 - Use tests, profiling, telemetry, and reproducible experiments to debug across system boundaries and verify correctness, performance, and recovery.

 - Make practical scope decisions, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and follow through from code to production. Teleport or comparable access-platform experience is helpful; strong engineering and production ownership matter more than knowing every tool.

title: Full Stack Software Engineer, Monetization Platform
description:
About the Team

As AI becomes capable of doing more useful work, the way people access and pay for it needs to evolve. Monetization Platform is a new team within Growth building the systems and experiences that make that possible across the entire suite of OpenAI products. Our mission is to make powerful AI easier to access, its value easier to understand, and new ways of using it easier to bring to market.

We work where product experience, platform architecture, and business strategy meet. A new plan or pricing model can change what customers can accomplish—and requires careful engineering across eligibility, entitlements, usage, and subscriptions. We turn that complexity into capabilities that product teams can build on and experiences that customers can trust.

Working with Product, Design, Finance, Financial Engineering, and Data Science, we’re shaping a platform that can evolve alongside our models and products. This is an opportunity to help define a new team’s technical direction and build systems that expand what OpenAI can offer.

 

About the Role

We’re looking for experienced Staff+ and Senior engineers who combine full-stack product instincts with strong backend and systems depth. You’ll help decide what to build, establish the architecture, and carry ideas through to working products—from a customer’s first interaction with a plan to the services that determine what they can access and use.

The work spans new pricing and packaging capabilities, plan and usage experiences, and the shared UIs and tools that make launches repeatable. You’ll partner closely with Financial Engineering to connect these capabilities to subscription and billing systems, keeping customer access and state consistent as offerings evolve.

You’ll have substantial ownership over technical decisions and delivery in an area where the roadmap is still taking shape. Your impact will show up in the experiences you ship, the engineering work you eliminate from future launches, and the opportunities your systems make possible.

 

In this role, you will:

 - Define and build shared pricing and packaging capabilities, including plan configuration, eligibility, entitlement integrations, and usage allowances.

 - Create intuitive plan and usage experiences across the stack, connecting polished interfaces to product APIs and backend services.

 - Turn new commercial ideas into working prototypes and experiments with Product, Finance, and Data Science, then use what you learn to guide the next iteration.

 - Design integrations with Financial Engineering that preserve correct access and subscription state through plan changes, migrations, asynchronous updates, and partial failures.

 - Build reusable components and configuration tools that let teams launch offerings with less custom engineering and fewer dependencies.

 - Take responsibility for production quality through migration planning, staged rollouts, testing, monitoring, and recovery paths.

 - Shape the technical roadmap, make clear tradeoffs between immediate launches and shared foundations, and develop other engineers through code and design reviews.

 

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have set architectural direction and delivered significant projects involving multiple teams, while remaining an active contributor to the code.

 - Bring depth in backend or distributed systems and can work across the APIs and interfaces that turn those systems into useful products.

 - Reason rigorously about data models, lifecycle transitions, consistency, concurrency, and what happens when an operation fails or runs twice.

 - Have taken loosely defined customer or business problems through discovery, implementation, and production operation.

 - Combine product intuition with experimentation and analysis, and care about whether customers understand and benefit from what you build.

 - Enjoy establishing new capabilities: choosing an initial design, shipping something useful, and improving it as the problem becomes clearer.

 - Build alignment across disciplines, explain technical choices clearly, and help teammates take on greater responsibility.

Experience with pricing, subscriptions, entitlements, usage-based products, billing integrations, or growth platforms would be especially valuable. We also welcome engineers whose experience building demanding product or platform systems prepares them to learn this domain.

title: Full-Stack Engineer — Systems Conductor
description: About Bold Business Bold Business is an AI-first, delivery-first company building production-grade enterprise software, automation engines, and autonomous agent infrastructure. AI coding environments (Cursor, Claude Code CLI, OpenClaw / Hermes Agents / Grokbot / other personal agent harnesses, and custom Model Context Protocol servers) are our native workspace, not a novelty. We expect you to command agents to write boilerplate, scaffold routes, and draft test suites. You provide the system architecture, the security guardrails, and the rigorous critical review. Speed from agents, judgment from you. Collaborative by Default. Every change is strictly peer-reviewed through pull requests. Documentation and automated unit tests ship in the same PR as the code. Blockers get raised early, not discovered at review. We value highly legible, standardized architectures that outlive their author's immediate attention — brilliant work that only its author understands is a liability here, not an asset. What You'll Do Architect schema-first features: design strict API boundaries, typed contracts, and database schemas first, providing the structure background AI agents need to implement features safely Build and secure module workflows: own recruiter and admin interfaces (screens, tables, profiles, forms, filters, dashboards), REST endpoints, and PostgreSQL relational workflows — with business security and authorization policies strictly enforced at the data layer Establish codebase context: build and use MCP servers and AST-based dependency graphs to give developer agents standardized, structured access to our repositories Orchestrate quality loops: set up local testing environments and containerized CI/CD checks where background agents automatically execute test runs, linting, and type validation before any merge Engage directly with stakeholders: sit with non-technical stakeholders to translate messy operational processes into clean, executable technical requirements — and keep them in the loop as the work progresses Stabilize and maintain the platform: production defects, small-to-medium gaps, and reporting migration support as Power BI is retired Review and be reviewed: give and receive pull-request review as a normal working rhythm, with test evidence on every ticket Non-Negotiables We'll ask you to demonstrate all of the following — come ready with real examples: Active agentic developer loop. You've transitioned beyond copy-pasting code blocks from a browser window. You can walk us through your CLI-native agentic loop: how you coordinate agents, what parameters and guardrails you set, and — specifically — a time you caught and patched an LLM hallucination before it shipped. "I've tried Copilot" is not this. Collaboration you can prove. A working history of PR reviews given and received, documentation you wrote that someone else actually used, and a time you escalated a blocker early instead of grinding on it alone. We will check for this specifically. Full-stack competency, production-grade. Strong React/TypeScript and Python/FastAPI experience on real systems in real use — not tutorials or side scripts. Database schema and security mastery. Highly fluent in PostgreSQL — schema design, migrations, indexing, transactional isolation. You understand why hiding a button in React is not an authorization control; authorization is enforced in the data layer. Clean systems architecture. You build robust, decoupled state machines (FastAPI, React state, background queues) that gracefully isolate, log, and recover from real-world API and network failures. Enterprise systems awareness. You've designed, maintained, or operated within ERP-class platforms (SAP, Oracle, Workday, NetSuite, or comparable) — or can clearly demonstrate how they work and why they matter: integrated data, standardized process, and a single operational source of truth. You'll help build a platform that plays exactly this role, so you need to understand what it replaces and what it must not break. True Agile and continuous improvement. Not standup theater — iterative delivery, working software shipped in small increments, retrospectives that actually change how the team works. Come ready to describe a real process improvement you drove based on what a sprint or a failure taught you. End-to-end micro-project ownership. You'll run micro-projects through their full lifecycle: planning and requirements gathering with stakeholders, implementation, testing, and maintenance afterward — documenting your work and processes clearly enough that another team member can be trained to support and back up what you built without you in the room. Come ready to walk us through one project you carried from first conversation to steady-state maintenance. Strong English communication, written and spoken. You'll operate in a U.S.-based team environment and explain technical decisions to non-technical stakeholders. Nice to Have Hands-on experience with OpenClaw, Hermes Agents, or Grokbot agent platforms Familiarity with LangGraph or stateful multi-agent orchestration Operations-heavy SaaS experience (recruiting, workforce management, ATS, or CRM) Multi-tenant application experience AWS exposure (EC2, RDS, S3, cloud logs) Data imports, deduplication, search/filter interfaces, operational reporting Experience joining a codebase mid-flight and getting productive fast What This Role Is A hands-on builder-conductor role with defined module ownership AI-accelerated delivery with human judgment on every merge A high-performing team operating model: review, documentation, and early communication are the job, not overhead What This Role Is Not Not a solo-operator role — if your best work happens when nobody sees it until it's done, this will be a bad fit Not an ML research role Not a role where AI tools are optional Compensation & Logistics Compensation based on experience. Standard options package per company policy. Target start: Immediately Final Note We will go deep into your past work — what you built, why you built it that way, what broke, and who else could run it after you. The engineers who thrive here are the ones whose systems outlive their attention: documented, reviewed, and understood by the team. Bold Business — AI-First. Delivery-First. Team-First.
